feed.title: What changed on Common Shade
feed.subtitle: Each reviewed change to the free evidence base on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia

entry.title: Signals shows the next step for each promise, and a weekly search looks for what it is missing
entry.summary: Each open commitment on Signals now shows the next step its sources describe and who made it. A weekly search of public feeds proposes developments the page has not yet tracked, for a person to review, and a grid shows the records kept for each place and when it was last searched.

entry.title: Signals shows each source's own words, and appears on every country, city and action page
entry.summary: Each checked piece of evidence on Signals now shows the sentence the source check found, and each commitment its dated path. Country, city and action pages show what is moving there, and State of the field lets each reader group read for its own question and keeps every open question in one running list.

entry.title: Signals opens with what moved, and both briefings can be followed without visiting
entry.summary: Signals now opens with the steps dated in the last 45 days and the dates coming up, so a phone reader reaches the first development within the first screen rather than after more than seven, and the page stays light as records grow. Signals, its scheduled dates and State of the field each have a feed or calendar, and every edition has three reading depths, a chat version and its own share image.

entry.title: Funding landscape, open calls and careers, checked against official pages
entry.summary: Funding for heat work is easy to misread: a funder is not an open call, a programme budget is not an award, and a tender is not a grant. The money page now opens with programmes and how each can be reached, and two new pages list calls and careers with application status and verification kept apart, so a closed or unconfirmed record never reads as open.

entry.title: Heat strain measured in Asian field work, beside the cotton page
entry.summary: No study has measured heat strain among cotton workers in Asia, so the cotton page now sets out what researchers found in neighbouring work: rice and sugarcane fields, farming villages and salt pans in India, Thailand, Viet Nam, Malaysia and Sri Lanka. It keeps strain, symptoms, kidneys, output and the gaps in the research apart, and names what a cotton study could measure.

entry.title: Heat from field to factory: cotton, informal work and who can stop
entry.summary: A new page follows cotton from field preparation and hand-picking through yards and ginning to the factory, keeping heat on people, heat on the crop and harm to livelihoods apart. It asks who can actually stop work in the heat, lists measures with who acts and who pays, and links both ways with Heat inside factories.

entry.title: The India archive adds Jalgaon's climate action plan, with its heat chapter
entry.summary: Jalgaon City Municipal Corporation's climate action plan, co-developed with Mahila Housing Trust, joins the India heat action plan archive. It is recorded as a heat plan inside a wider plan: its heat chapter includes ward-level heat-vulnerability mapping and cool-roof pilots, and it recommends passing a formal heat action plan.

entry.title: Heat inside factories: sources, protection and an intervention library
entry.summary: A new feature follows heat by task, place and time through a garment factory, explaining why two people in the same building can face very different heat. Its library of measures, from roofs and steam repair to paid breaks and buyer purchasing, gives each one's evidence type and limits, with a finder, comparison, worked examples and a worksheet for workers and managers.

entry.title: From what clinicians report to the guidance they can already use
entry.summary: The clinicians' survey presented at COP31 now leads straight to India's own guidance on heat and pregnancy, published by the health ministry and UNFPA India in May 2026 for healthcare providers and community health workers. It sits beside the survey on Signals and Who is at risk, and among the guides for heat-safe pregnancy and newborn care.

entry.title: COP31, fourth check-in: what maternity and newborn clinicians report seeing
entry.summary: A survey commissioned by Wellcome, presented at COP31, asked 1,000 clinicians in pregnancy and newborn care in five countries, India among them, what heat is doing to the women and babies they care for. It joins the watch as a finding, labelled as clinicians' reports rather than measured outcomes, and the pregnant women group on Who is at risk now carries it too.

entry.title: Signals follows two new state heat institutions in India
entry.summary: Tamil Nadu's Heat Resilience Centre, set up with the UK, and Maharashtra's Centre of Excellence for heat resilience and sustainable cooling join Signals, each on the step its sources show, so the site can record whether they deliver.

entry.title: How India's heat policy is changing: state examples, guides and the money gap
entry.summary: NRDC's 2026 review of heat policy in India and three NIUA documents add state and city examples to five actions, practical guides on heat plans, cooling centres, city plans and finance, a global figure on how little urban climate finance goes to adaptation, and NRDC to the heat network.

entry.title: NIUA's learning notes for city officials: showing results, and where heat lands
entry.summary: Two learning notes from India's National Institute of Urban Affairs add a guide to showing results on three cooling actions, a free training series, a passage on heat within a city, and NIUA's Climate Centre for Cities to the heat network.

entry.title: COP31, third check-in: a cooling roadmap and WHO's El Niño plan
entry.summary: Governments backed a voluntary roadmap on heat resilience and cooling at the Cooling Ministerial, with new support announced, and WHO set out its El Niño health plan. Each joins the watch on the step it has reached.

entry.title: Dry soils and heat arriving together, from a daily global record
entry.summary: A data set paper published in November 2026, checked against the publisher's open PDF, finds dry and hot conditions occurring together more often since 2000 in several hotspot regions, faster than either alone would suggest, with China's Yangtze River Basin rising from 10 to 21 events per grid square. The map's drying soils entry now carries it with its limits: a reanalysis estimate that leaves out irrigation and reports no country result for South or Southeast Asia.

entry.title: A daily heat data set covering the region, in the Heat Tool Finder
entry.summary: The Heat Tool Finder now lists CHIRTS-ERA5 from the Climate Hazards Center, a quasi-global daily grid of maximum and minimum temperature, heat index and WBGT, checked against the provider's own page. It is listed as an estimate for analysts, not tested and not locally validated, with its licence not yet verified.

entry.title: Heat-safe work: protections that workers cannot use
entry.summary: Heat-safe work now carries a watch-out, checked against an Oxfam America post: in Hong Kong some outdoor cleaners given cooling vests were stopped from wearing them because the vests covered a company logo, and in Cambodia workers whose unions had bargained over heat exposure were better protected. Equipment and rules help only where workers have the room to use them.

entry.title: The year's climate findings: India's April heat, early warnings and El Niño's health risks
entry.summary: Two Signals records now carry more from WMO's State of the Climate Update 2026, checked against its press release: an estimated 146.5 million people in India exposed to extreme heat in an April 2026 heatwave, countries reporting multi-hazard early warning systems up from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025, and WHO's first classification of El Niño's anticipated health impacts as a health emergency.

entry.title: A drawing beside Heat-safe work: the cooling vest
entry.summary: Heat-safe work on the actions page now has an illustrative drawing beside its watch-out: an outdoor cleaner sweeping in the heat puts on a cooling vest from its stand, then hangs it back up. It adds no new claim; the checked sentence and its source stay above it, and the drawing loads only when a reader presses play.

entry.title: Plan a response: save the whole plan as a file, and open it again
entry.summary: A plan made on Plan a response can now be saved as a file with everything in it, owners, notes and money included, and a colleague can open that file in their own browser to keep working. Nothing is sent anywhere: the file stays with whoever saves it.

entry.title: The heat network: 40 more organisations link to their own heat work
entry.summary: Forty more organisations in the heat network now link to the page on their own site that shows their heat work, not just their homepage. Each link was opened on GitHub and held the word it rests on; six that did not open or did not hold it were left as they were.

entry.title: Signals now shows what the evidence confirms for each promise
entry.summary: Each commitment on Signals is now tracked deliverable by deliverable, so an office, a research fund and a future plan no longer share one status, and every milestone names its sources, what each establishes and whether the site's source check confirmed it. Secondary reports and pages that only opened are shown as such, nothing missing is called failed, and a filtered view can be shared, saved, printed or downloaded.

entry.title: State of the field becomes a dated, sourced monthly briefing with an archive
entry.summary: Each edition now makes one argument and states what it rests on, keeps apart when something happened and when Common Shade reviewed it, and shows for every claim its source, what that source establishes and what it does not. Editions keep what they said at publication, corrections are dated in the edition and on the corrections page, and each edition has a stable link, a print layout and a Markdown briefing.

entry.title: How heat is reported: one explorer over both collections, with each reviewed article's reporting trail
entry.summary: The page now explains how a multilingual pilot complicated its first reading, and lets readers find every article across countries, languages and collections, see what the review found in each, compare stories on the same protection and build a source-linked reporting question. Missing information reads not recorded or not assessed, never as a failure.

entry.title: Heat plans and the heatwave longer than any on record
entry.summary: A 2026 modelling study, checked against its open full text, finds that some future heatwaves in India and Pakistan could outlast the region's recent record even with low emissions. The heat action plan action now carries that as something to watch for, and the learning agenda asks whether plans, budgets and cooling spaces could keep running through one.

entry.title: Humid heat in Southeast Asia, beside the longer heatwaves
entry.summary: A 2025 study measuring humid heat stress across Southeast Asia, checked against its open full text, projects that far more people could face a week or more of extreme humid heat, with 6 to 9 hours of severe heat stress a day in Myanmar, Thailand and Cambodia in peak months. It sits beside the study of longer heatwaves, which covers daily maximum temperature in India and Pakistan only.

entry.title: Actions chosen in Build protection now carry into a plan
entry.summary: A reader chose paid rest breaks in Build protection, followed the link to Plan a response and found an empty plan. The actions now carry across and join whatever the plan already holds, without replacing any notes, and each line says which actions it came from.

entry.title: The Heat Assembly: a game about who can use heat protection
entry.summary: A shaded hall can be paid for and open, and still be out of reach for a porter who would lose a paid turn by leaving the queue. Played alone or around a table over four rounds of heat, the game makes funded, open and usable different things, shows each person's outcome without a score, and lets players replay one decision to see whose day changes.

entry.title: The Philippines' heat advisories: two more checked reports, and the open question named
entry.summary: Two news reports, checked word for word, add detail to the Philippines' October 2026 labour advisories on heat: duties that step up with the same four heat index levels the site already shows, and compensation for heat stroke, cramps and exhaustion, with other heat illnesses that may also qualify where the link to work is shown. The advisory texts themselves were not read, because the department's pages turn away automated checks, so the record still says so.

entry.title: A policy brief on heat-ready social security, with examples from across Asia
entry.summary: When heat stops work, a day off can mean a day without pay. The brief sets out five ways social security could cushion that choice, with examples from China, Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Hong Kong, the Philippines, the United Arab Emirates, India, Thailand and Viet Nam, examples from elsewhere labelled as such, the traps to avoid and options step by step.
